To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the soil zone and in-situ sources of organic matter are the main carbon sources for groundwater DOC in this confined methanogenic system.
the soil zone and organic rich sediments in the matrix of the aquifer are the major DOC sources in the aquifer.
the DOC cycle in a regional methanogenic confined aquifer is controlled by both an in-situ source of DOC and a soil source.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical and carbon isotopic (14C, 13C and 13C) composition of the dissolved organic carbon pool (DOC) in a regional confined aquifer.

the origin of DOC and CH4, the role of organic rich sediments in the DOC cycle, the fate of DOC in a regional confined aquifer and the importance of DOC on the carbon cycle of a methanogenic aquifers.
the DOC cycle and the fate of DOC in groundwater in a regional confined aquifer system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DOC in groundwater is a mixture of a soil derived DOC fraction, an in-situ derived DOC fraction, a bedrock derived DOC fraction and a DOC fraction derived from microbial activity.
soil organic matter is the primary source of DOC in the upper part of the groundwater system, whereas in the lower part the aquifer matrix acts as an important in-situ DOC reservoir.
the DOC cycle in the regional aquifer is controlled by a combination of in-situ DOC production and DOC transport from the soil zone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

DOC in groundwater is a mixture of terrestrial organic matter, which is the primary carbon source of DOC in the aquifer, and of in-situ organic matter, which contributes to a large extent to the DOC pool in central part of the aquifer.

DOC in the regional confined aquifer of the Paris Basin is mainly composed of terrestrial organic matter, which is mainly supplied from the soil zone in areas close to the recharge zones and from in-situ sources in central areas of the groundwater flow.
the DOC pool in this aquifer has two main sources: (1) soil organic matter in the upper part of the aquifer; and (2) a terrestrial source in the central part.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combined use of DOC chemical and isotopic data is a powerful tool to understand the origin and the fate of DOC in a groundwater system.
the combined use of chemical (DOC concentration) and isotopic data (13C, 14C) can provide a better understanding of the DOC source and fate in groundwater.
the use of chemical and carbon isotopic tracers is a powerful tool to unravel the DOC cycle in groundwater.
